system_description.narrative_title: Middle East conflict disrupts global oil flows and fuels market turmoil
system_description.narrative_summary: Escalation of warfare around Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea chokepoints is disrupting seaborne oil and gas flows, driving price volatility and creating windfalls for energy firms and commodity traders. States and firms are responding with military coalitions, tanker purchases and rerouting, while inventories, refining and LNG trade patterns shift — producing wider economic effects (inflation, interest-rate sensitivity) and strategic realignments. The dynamic couples short-term supply shocks with longer-term shifts in trade routes, security arrangements and energy sourcing.
system_description.scope: Seaborne oil and gas production, storage and transport (Hormuz, Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb), global crude and refined product markets and prices, energy firms and trading houses, national strategic responses (military coalitions, sanctions, procurement), tanker and shipping operations, refinery and LNG flows.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical–energy–economic system (global trade, finance and international security)
adjacent_subsystems: Global commodity & financial markets (ETFs, traders, banks)
National energy policy and OPEC+ decision-making

variables.name: Seaborne oil & gas flow rate
variables.description: Volume of crude oil and natural gas (including LNG) transported by sea per unit time across global maritime routes.

variables.name: Maritime chokepoint security
variables.description: Overall level of security, access stability and navigational risk at major maritime chokepoints (e.g., narrow straits and canals).

variables.name: Crude oil price level
variables.description: Market price level for benchmark crude oil measured in currency per barrel.

variables.name: Refined product price level
variables.description: Market price level for refined petroleum products (diesel, gasoline, jet fuel) measured in currency per unit.

variables.name: Oil & gas price volatility
variables.description: Rate and magnitude of short‑term fluctuations in oil and gas prices over a defined horizon.

variables.name: Tanker fleet utilization rate
variables.description: Proportion of available tanker tonnage actively employed in seaborne energy transport over time.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting rate
variables.description: Rate at which planned seaborne energy shipments are diverted to longer or alternative routes per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime attack incidence rate
variables.description: Frequency of hostile incidents (attacks, interdictions, strikes) affecting energy shipping and related assets per unit time.

variables.name: War risk premium level
variables.description: Market‑perceived extra cost or premium (insurance, contract pricing, risk allowances) applied to shipping and energy transactions due to conflict risk.

variables.name: Strategic and commercial stockpiles
variables.description: Aggregate volume of petroleum held in strategic reserves and commercial inventories at a point in time.

variables.name: Refinery throughput rate
variables.description: Rate at which crude oil is processed into refined products across the refining system per unit time.

variables.name: LNG trade flow rate
variables.description: Volume of liquefied natural gas traded across international sea routes per unit time.

variables.name: Commodity trading concentration
variables.description: Degree of market concentration and market power among intermediaries and traders in energy commodity markets.

variables.name: Fuel contribution to inflation
variables.description: Rate at which changes in energy prices are contributing to consumer price inflation over time.

variables.name: Shipping and storage capacity
variables.description: Total available tanker transport tonnage and afloat/onshore storage capacity for seaborne energy at a point in time.

variables.name: Naval/military presence level
variables.description: Aggregate deployed naval and military assets and patrol intensity in maritime zones relevant to energy transit.

catalysts.title: Saudi-led multinational maritime defence coalition forms
catalysts.description: Saudi Arabia's announced coalition will deploy coordinated patrols and escorts to protect Red Sea shipping, changing security posture and insurance pricing.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Saudi Arabia unveils/seeks multinational maritime defence coalition; Saudi joins US strikes.

catalysts.title: Houthi attacks and potential Red Sea fees persist
catalysts.description: Continued Houthi strikes and talk of imposing transit fees in the Red Sea will sustain elevated attack rates and shipping diversion costs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Houthis attacking, considering fees; Saudi seeks coalition to protect Red Sea shipping.

catalysts.title: Iran threats and interdictions in Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Iran's threats to stop or seize ships and recent tanker attacks near Hormuz heighten transit risk and may force rerouting through longer corridors.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Iran threatens to choke off routes, stops ships in Hormuz; tankers near Oman come under fire.

catalysts.title: Reported tanker incidents off Oman (UKMTO)
catalysts.description: UKMTO-reported incidents near Oman indicate near-term continued hostile actions that could temporarily disrupt local transit and insurance rates.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: UKMTO reports two tanker incidents off Oman; tankers near Oman come under fire.

catalysts.title: QatarEnergy buys US LNG cargoes to offset Hormuz disruption
catalysts.description: QatarEnergy's purchase of US LNG cargoes and re‑deployment of LNG tankers will re-route LNG trade flows and absorb some displaced demand.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: QatarEnergy buys 33 US LNG cargoes; QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exits Hormuz.

catalysts.title: OPEC+ may keep lifting output quotas
catalysts.description: OPEC+ signalling continued quota increases could raise seaborne crude volumes and exert downward pressure on benchmark prices despite conflict-driven premiums.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: OPEC+ may keep lifting its oil output quotas as the Iran war broadens.

catalysts.title: India increases spot oil purchases
catalysts.description: Indian refiners boosting spot crude buys will raise short‑term seaborne imports and add to inventory accumulation through summer demand management.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Indian Oil Corp boost spot oil buy amid Middle East crisis.

catalysts.title: Turkey-Iraq one‑year oil pipeline deal begins
catalysts.description: A signed one‑year pipeline agreement will shift some crude away from seaborne routes, lowering tanker loads and rerouting volumes onto land.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Turkey, Iraq sign one-year oil pipeline deal.

catalysts.title: Oil spill from shadow fleet tanker off Oman spreads
catalysts.description: A spreading spill from a shadow‑fleet tanker could force local route restrictions and cleanup, temporarily reducing throughput and tightening product markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Oil spill from shadow fleet tanker spreading off Oman, satellite images show.

catalysts.title: US–Saudi strikes and allied actions escalate
catalysts.description: Continued allied strikes on Iran‑backed groups will raise regional military activity and can provoke retaliatory attacks on energy shipping and infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Saudi joins US strikes; oil jumps after fresh strikes; Trump threats escalate responses.
